boundary_decision.status: accepted as a source-qualified taxon concept
boundary_decision.rationale: The model represents a stable conceptual biological grouping according to a named classification and release. Names, organisms, populations, specimens, occurrences, sequences, publications, nomenclatural acts, habitats, distributions and conservation assessments remain distinct linked objects.

decisions.rationale: The same name may denote different circumscriptions and a concept may carry several name usages, so name text is never sufficient concept identity.
Circumscription, placement, acceptance and synonymy are assertions made by a named classification, checklist, revision or database release.

decisions.disposition: accepted as parallel truths with mappings
decisions.rationale: Source classifications remain intact and cross-source reconciliation records congruence, inclusion, overlap, disjointness or uncertainty without last-write-wins collapse.
Rank is source-qualified and may be absent where the source classification deliberately uses rankless placement.
Codes govern names, typification and acts for different organismal domains but do not determine taxonomic circumscription or scientific acceptance.
Physical, spatial, custody and observation properties belong to organisms, specimens, occurrences, sequences and evidence records, not to the abstract taxon concept.
Diagnostic descriptions and differential characters need applicability, observation conditions, evidence, confidence and confusing alternatives rather than unqualified prose.
Split, lump, boundary and placement changes create successor versions and explicit change sets while cited predecessors remain resolvable.

decisions.disposition: accepted as related but non-identical projections
decisions.rationale: TCS explicitly separates concepts, names, mappings and types, while broad Darwin Core Taxon records require a declared concept-versus-name-usage interpretation.

decisions.concept: Catalogue of Life, GBIF and NCBI
decisions.rationale: Each service owns its identifiers, releases and coverage and cannot be treated as a universal arbiter of all taxonomy.
